tasks.short: Collect prisoners' requests, build the day schedule, check separation rules, tell prisoners their schedule and confirm slots with departments.

steps.what: Officer collects paper request slips for library visits, family visits and appointments
Officer arranges daily schedules for prisoners on a spreadsheet
Officer checks the schedule against separation and security rules
Officer tells each prisoner their work assignments and appointments in person
Officer phones the library, counselling and work departments to confirm slots

tasks.design: Prisoners enter requests on the unit's self-service terminal linked to the prison information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and a planning board proposes the day schedule from department slots and capacity. Fixed rules flag clashes with separation orders and security restrictions for the officer to resolve; prisoners see their schedule on the terminal and departments see their bookings, while the officer still explains changes in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were paper slips and the schedule a spreadsheet checked by memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Self-service terminals and rule-based planning boards exist for institutions; no AI is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Separation orders must be complete; some prisoners cannot use a terminal.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which two prisoners must never be in the library together, even if no rule says so yet.
tasks.altitude: The officer checks a proposed schedule instead of building it.

reach.learn: Whether shared slots cut double bookings.

evidence.claim: Prisons in some countries use self-service terminals for prisoner requests and schedules.
Rule-based scheduling uses no AI; profiling-based risk tools for offenders are high-risk.

assumptions: Boundary: from requests to the confirmed day schedule; transport to court is outside.
Input contract: department slots kept by each department; separation orders and restrictions recorded by the security office; fallback is paper slips and the spreadsheet.
Department and security office time is outside the officer's savings.
unknowns: Whether the prison has unit terminals.
research_questions: Do separation clashes fall with rule checks?

incremental.description: Officer helps prisoners use the terminal.
Security office keeps separation orders current in the system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Units with many prisoners who cannot use terminals keep paper slips.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take over custody and check the committal order, search the new prisoner, explain rules and rights, ask screening questions, assign a cell and complete the intake checklist.

steps.what: Officer takes over custody from transport and checks the committal order on paper
Officer searches the convicted individual and their belongings
Officer explains house rules and rights to the new prisoner
Officer asks the screening questions on health and suicide risk
Officer assigns a cell and issues clothing and items from a paper list
Officer completes the paper intake checklist to process the arrival into prison

tasks.design: The committal order arrives electronically in the prison information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) before the transport, and house rules and rights are shown from a library of approved translations and short videos while the officer explains. Cell occupancy shows on screen, issued items are logged by scan, and the intake checklist is a screen that fills as steps are done; searching and screening stay fully manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Committal papers arrived with the prisoner, and intake was paper lists and checklists.
tasks.enabler_now: Justice chain partners can exchange orders electronically; translated information libraries are simple to keep.
tasks.still_hard: Intake is a tense moment; screening for suicide risk needs a person's full attention.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a new prisoner is not coping and alerting the nurse at once.

reach.learn: Whether screening answers reach the nurse faster on screen.

evidence.claim: Justice chain partners can exchange committal orders electronically.
Prisoners must be told their rights and the house rules in a language they understand.

assumptions: Boundary: from taking over custody to the completed intake; the medical intake by the nurse is outside.
Input contract: committal orders sent by the prosecution through the chain exchange; translations approved by the prison's legal office; item barcodes from the stores; fallback is paper.
Searching and screening do not change.
Nurse time is outside the officer's savings.
research_questions: Do translated videos improve new prisoners' understanding of rules?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of intake is searching, explaining and screening in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Brief the shift, assign posts, walk the units and support officers, handle incidents and write the shift report.

steps.what: Senior officer briefs the shift team on the day's events
Senior officer assigns posts and tasks to officers on a whiteboard
Senior officer walks the units to supervise and coordinate work of other correctional officers
Senior officer handles incidents and calls in extra staff
Senior officer writes the shift report for management

tasks.design: A post plan in the prison information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) is proposed from the roster and each officer's qualifications by fixed rules, and the senior officer adjusts it. The shift report is built from the unit logs and incident reports for the senior officer to complete; briefing, walking the units and handling incidents stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Posts were planned on a whiteboard and shift reports written from memory and logs.
tasks.enabler_now: Rosters and logs are digital; rule-based post plans and report templates are plain software.
tasks.still_hard: Staff shortages break any plan; the report needs the senior officer's view of the shift.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a tired team steady through a difficult night.

reach.learn: Whether built reports show recurring problems.

evidence.claim: Rosters, logs and incident reports can feed rule-based post plans and report templates.
Systems that record which officer did what can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: one shift from briefing to report; rostering is outside.
Input contract: roster and qualifications kept by the planning office; unit logs from the officers; fallback is the whiteboard.
Post plans are rule-based, not ranking officers.
Planning office time is outside the senior officer's savings.
research_questions: Do built shift reports miss anything managers need?

already_counted.description: Senior officer completes the built shift report.

incremental.description: Senior officer learns the post plan screen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is leading people on the floor.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain the procedure, take fingerprints on the scanner, retake poor prints, enter personal details, read the identity result and file the receipt.

steps.what: Officer explains the procedure and takes fingerprints of prisoners on the scanner
Officer checks print quality and retakes poor prints
Officer types the person's details into the fingerprint system
Officer reads the identity result from the national system
Officer files the printed receipt in the prisoner's paper file

tasks.design: The fingerprint station takes the person's details from the prison information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of retyping them, and the identity result is stored on the prisoner record, so no paper receipt is filed. Taking prints, judging quality and reading the result stay with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fingerprint station was a separate system with its own data entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Fingerprint stations can be linked to records systems.
tasks.still_hard: Biometric data need the strictest access; a link must not widen who can see it.
tasks.human_edge: Getting usable prints from someone who does not want to cooperate, calmly.

reach.learn: Whether linked stations cut entry errors.

evidence.claim: Fingerprint stations can take personal details from a linked records system.
Fingerprinting a person in custody is not real-time remote biometric identification in public, which the AI Act restricts.

assumptions: Boundary: from taking prints to the result stored; identity disputes are outside.
Input contract: personal details from the prisoner record kept by the records office; link set up by the information manager; fallback is typing.
Taking prints and reading results do not change.
Information manager time is outside the officer's savings.
unknowns: Whether the fingerprint station supports a link.
research_questions: Do typing errors in print records fall?

incremental.description: Officer checks the linked details before scanning.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is taking the prints in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The correctional officer keeps searches, screening, supervision and prints; scheduling, intake paperwork and reports shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking proposed schedules against what they know of the unit
role.ambitious_version: An officer whose schedules and intake records are ready before the prisoner arrives.
